transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-14 11:00 AM UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom - pilot readout
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Andre Lewis (Redwood), Priya Shah (Vireo Lead ML), Tom Alvarez (Vireo Platform), Ellen Wu (Vireo SRE), Matt (Vireo procurement)
---
Summary (auto): Redwood pilot shows 12-18% lower median latency vs incumbent, 20-30% lower cost per token in warm-cached workloads, but cold-start tail remains an issue.
---
[00:00] Jordan Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh let's run through the numbers we sent. quick reminder, I'm Jordan, AE, maya is our se who ran the bench.
[00:22] Priya Shah: thanks jordan, and thanks maya. we pulled up the spreadsheet, so feel free to jump in, tom is here to listen for infra notes.
[00:37] Maya Chen: cool, i'll start with the high-level. so this week we compared your baseline provider -- the one you called "incumbent" -- against our hosted pilot + dedicated-approx run. we did the same model variant, 13B-ish, quant4 and int8 path for the dedicated sim.
[01:05] Tom Alvarez: quick q, was the baseline run on same gpu type? i think you mentioned they used A100s and we used A10Gs earlier?
[01:15] Maya Chen: right, good call. baseline was A100 v4 on their managed endpoint, our hosted pilot was on A10G-heavy but with kernel-level optimizations. so not perfectly apples-to-apples; we included a normalized sheet column that adjusts for peak clocks.
[01:38] Ellen Wu: the normalization math looked OK but the variance on the 95th line is puzzling, can you explain the tail better?
[01:47] Maya Chen: yeah so median is straightforward 40-55 ms lower on our runs across typical 512 token prompts. the 95th/99th percentiles tighten after KV cache warm -- once prefix caching kicks in. cold starts, though, show spikes up to +400 ms, which is similar to the incumbent when their cold paths hit.
[02:12] Priya Shah: when you say "KV cache warm" do you mean the prefix cache on session reuse? we're doing long conversations in prod, so warm is the common case.
[02:21] Maya Chen: exactly, session reuse and continuous KV cache yields much better SLOs. we also saw batching improvements when token distribution is narrow.
[02:34] Jordan Park: i'll add that our smart routing can route to a compatible quantized variant if a dedicated is saturated; that reduces cost further.
[02:45] Tom Alvarez: cost question - the sheet shows 20-30% lower unit cost if we accept quant4. what's the quality delta?
[02:55] Priya Shah: yes we need a quality number; our evals are particularly sensitive to hallucination on that model.
[03:05] Maya Chen: for the prompts you gave us, quant4 introduced negligible ROUGE/EM drop, about 1.2% on average in our internal evals. but we should run it against your golden prompts.
[03:18] Priya Shah: we'll share the 200 prompt set after the call.
[03:25] Matt: procurement - any impact on data residency or logs if we move to dedicated slots?
[03:31] Jordan Park: dedicated slots give you isolation and a private subnet option in Redwood Private; logs are kept per your retention and we can align to your KMS. we'll attach the SOC2 and network diagram.
[03:45] Ellen Wu: do you have HSM integrations? our compliance team wants to make sure keys never leave our KMS.
[03:53] Maya Chen: yes, KMS/HSM is supported in Private; small note, our hosted pinned keys flow is different — we'll send the matrix.
[04:07] [crosstalk] Tom Alvarez: and SLA? / Jordan Park: SLA for dedicated is SLA-backed, yeah 99.9 for latency targets we negotiate.
[04:20] [05:00] Maya Chen: back to bench. we instrumented token throughput (QPS) and end-to-end latency. for warm-cache scenarios, your peak ran at ~620 qps with median latency ~110ms, while baseline peaked at ~510 qps with median 140ms. that gave us roughly 18% better throughput in the same provisioned env.
[05:40] Priya Shah: nice. how consistent were those numbers over longer runs? we saw oscillations in our night windows.
[05:48] Maya Chen: over 2 hour runs they were consistent after warm-up, but the first 10-15 minutes had more variance due to cold kernels and JIT-ish warm ups on some vendor kernels.
[06:05] Jordan Park: note — we had one misconfig where batch_size was set to 4 vs the intended 8 in run #3; that made one sample look worse but we excluded it in the main sheet.
[06:20] Priya Shah: okay good to know.
[06:25] [07:00] Andre Lewis: we also did a routing experiment: when a node falls below latency SLO, smart routing pushed traffic to a quantized variant. tail latencies fell by 25% but cost per token went up 6% due to more CPU overhead on the fallback.
[07:22] Tom Alvarez: interesting tradeoff. so routing to a cheaper variant improves tail but increases per-token cost?
[07:30] Andre Lewis: it depends — in our sim the fallback variant had more CPU decode time which moved cost in that direction. the big win was availability during noisy neighbor events.
[07:43] Priya Shah: can the routing be traffic-split for canary? we want to test with 5% traffic first.
[07:50] Maya Chen: yes, we support canaries and A/B split with gradual rollouts.
[07:55] [08:30] Priya Shah: one item - our SRE saw a few 500-ish errors in the first 20m of the test. logs show socket reset; any idea?
[08:40] Ellen Wu: yeah we caught those too, wondering if that's networking or model oom.
[08:46] Maya Chen: my hunch is periodic OOM on their side due to long KV sequences; we saw occasional GC-like pauses when the KV cache grew beyond expected. we'll share flamegraph and heap traces.
[09:05] Jordan Park: action: we'll re-run that scen with a pinned kv policy to keep cache bounded.
[09:12] Priya Shah: good.
[09:18] [10:00] Tom Alvarez: about the cold-start spikes — is there a warm-pool option? can you keep workers warm?
[10:09] Maya Chen: yes, dedicated slots behave like warm pools. you can reserve min capacity and enable keep-alive which eliminates cold kernel spikes. that is the main reason teams choose dedicated for production.
[10:28] Matt: price delta?
[10:31] Jordan Park: i'll put numbers in a side-by-side: hosted pay-as-you-go vs reserved dedicated monthly. initial estimate shows ~12% higher fixed cost but consistent SLO and lower P99 overall.
[10:45] [12:00] Maya Chen: a couple oddities: one run had an unexpected IO stall when we pushed logs to your S3 -- turned out the endpoint DNS lookup had a small hiccup. we recommend using a regional endpoint and pre-resolving.
[12:21] Priya Shah: thanks, that's useful.
[12:30] [13:00] Priya Shah: quality again — you mentioned the quantized path had minimal impact, but can we see token-by-token diffs for a sample set?
[13:10] Maya Chen: absolutely, we'll produce a diff view and BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics per prompt.
[13:20] [15:00] Jordan Park: ok let's talk next steps, we proposed a 2-hour dedicated-slot uplift to simulate your production 1.2k qps window. we need approval for the uplift schedule.
[15:12] Priya Shah: we can do 5/25 or 5/26, prefer 5/25.
[15:20] Jordan Park: great, we'll tentatively book 5/25 02:00 UTC.
[15:27] Tom Alvarez: will you stream logs to our ELK? we need those for traceability.
[15:33] Andre Lewis: yes, we can stream and we'll redact sensitive tokens as per the agreed mask rules.
[15:40] [16:00] Matt: procurement again - any long-term commitments if we do a short uplift?
[16:08] Jordan Park: no, uplift is a short term reserved slot for the test; any longer reserved committed pricing would be a separate contract.
[16:18] Priya Shah: one ask from us: can you enable per-token cost breakdown in the console for the uplift? we want to see micro-costs during spike.
[16:25] Jordan Park: yes, console supports token-level cost and we'll turn on high-frequency metrics for that window.
[16:32] [20:00] Maya Chen: ok dataset note: priya will send the 200 prompts and the 3 golden examples; we'll run quant4/8 and base fp16 and return diffs.
[20:15] Priya Shah: sending after the call.
[20:20] Ellen Wu: curious, any known issues with our cloud provider? we're on GCP us-east1.
[20:27] Maya Chen: no blockers, we have regions there. one small caveat: if you use VPC peering with our hosted infra there are NAT timeout tweaks that sometimes cause resets; we'll share recommended sysctl tweaks.
[20:45] [25:00] Jordan Park: okay to recap: action items, maya to re-run kv-warm runs with 8k token tail, jordan to send pricing delta and SOC2, priya to send prompts, tom to validate uplift window.
[25:22] Priya Shah: yep, agreed.
[25:30] [30:00] Andre Lewis: final tech note — quantized kernel selection can change decode CPU patterns; if you see CPU dips, consider slight re-batching to smooth throughput.
[30:19] Tom Alvarez: thanks, that tip helps.
[30:25] [35:00] Priya Shah: any blockers on our side? not right now, just to confirm the uplift won't change our current contract terms.
[35:12] Jordan Park: confirmed, uplift is a test; procurement will get a short-term addendum if needed.
[35:25] [40:00] Priya Shah: one last question: if the uplift goes well, how long to spin up a private deployment? we might prefer Private for data residency.
[40:12] Maya Chen: standard on-prem/private setup is 6-8 weeks for full air-gapped with KMS and audit logs; with our marketplace regions it can be faster ~3-4 weeks depending on networking.
[40:30] Priya Shah: good to know.
[42:00] Jordan Park: great, we'll send the benchmark raw traces and flamegraphs by monday, and lock the 5/25 uplift. thanks everyone.
[42:22] Matt: thanks.
[42:30] Priya Shah: thanks team.
[47:40] [call ended]
